items.title: The base change where a map becomes zero is cut out by a closed subscheme, of finite presentation in the finite type case

items.difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the existence of a closed subscheme through which the test morphism factors and over which the map vanishes at source lines 1566-1575, label lemma-F-zero-somewhat-closed, whose proof occupies source lines 1577-1624. The proof is a genuine computation rather than a reduction: after cutting the space and the test scheme down to affine pieces it replaces the statement by a map of modules over a ring, and since the target module is flat it invokes Lazard's theorem to write each value of the map through a free module on which the value already dies after the given base change, collects the coefficients into an ideal, and checks that this ideal does the job. The finiteness statement is a second argument: the ideal is written as a filtered union of finitely generated ideals and the limit criterion picks one of them, which uses the finite type assumption and quasi-compactness of the support. The counted statement records neither the Lazard step nor the limit argument.
